body.en: Topic 3 unites circular geometry, analytical trigonometry, vector algebra, and wave mechanics. Core themes include radian geometry, triangle solving, double-angle identities, 2D vector scalar products, and sinusoidal modelling.
body.ar: Topic 3 unites circular الهندسة, analytical حساب المثلثات, المتجه الجبر, and wave mechanics. Core themes include radian الهندسة, المثلث solving, double-الزاوية المتطابقات, 2D المتجه scalar products, and sinusoidal modelling.

label.en: ● Level 1 Foundation — Radian Measure, Circle Mensuration & Unit Circle
label.ar: ● Level 1 Foundation — Radian Measure, الدائرة Mensuration & Unit الدائرة

body.en:
One radian (rad) is the angle subtended at the centre of a circle of radius \(r\) by an arc of length equal to \(r\). Because the circumference is \(2\pi r\), a complete revolution is \(2\pi\) radians:

\[ 2\pi \text{ rad} = 360^\circ \iff 1 \text{ rad} = \frac{180^\circ}{\pi} \approx 57.296^\circ, \quad 1^\circ = \frac{\pi}{180} \text{ rad}. \]

Circle Geometry Formulations (where \(\theta\) is in radians):

  • Arc Length: \[ s = r\theta. \]
  • Sector Area: \[ A_{\text{sector}} = \frac{1}{2}r^2\theta. \]
  • Segment Area: The region bounded by a chord and its arc: \[ A_{\text{segment}} = \frac{1}{2}r^2\theta - \frac{1}{2}r^2\sin\theta = \frac{1}{2}r^2(\theta - \sin\theta). \]

The Unit Circle: For any angle \(\theta\), the coordinates of the corresponding point on the unit circle \(x^2 + y^2 = 1\) are \((x, y) = (\cos\theta, \sin\theta)\), giving \(\tan\theta = \frac{y}{x} = \frac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}\). Signs follow the ASTC quadrant rule: All positive in Q1, Sine in Q2, Tangent in Q3, Cosine in Q4.
body.ar:
One radian (rad) is the الزاوية subtended at the centre of a الدائرة of نصف القطر \(r\) by an arc of length equal to \(r\). Because the circumference is \(2\pi r\), a complete revolution is \(2\pi\) radians:

\[ 2\pi \text{ rad} = 360^\circ \iff 1 \text{ rad} = \frac{180^\circ}{\pi} \approx 57.296^\circ, \quad 1^\circ = \frac{\pi}{180} \text{ rad}. \]

Circle الهندسة Formulations (حيث \(\theta\) is in radians):

  • Arc Length: \[ s = r\theta. \]
  • Sector المساحة: \[ A_{\text{sector}} = \frac{1}{2}r^2\theta. \]
  • Segment المساحة: The region bounded by a chord and its arc: \[ A_{\text{segment}} = \frac{1}{2}r^2\theta - \frac{1}{2}r^2\sin\theta = \frac{1}{2}r^2(\theta - \sin\theta). \]

The Unit الدائرة: For any الزاوية \(\theta\), the الإحداثيات of the corresponding point on the unit الدائرة \(x^2 + y^2 = 1\) are \((x, y) = (\cos\theta, \sin\theta)\), giving \(\tan\theta = \frac{y}{x} = \frac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}\). Signs follow the ASTC quadrant rule: All positive in Q1, Sine in Q2, Tangent in Q3, Cosine in Q4.

label.en: ● Level 2 Analytical Tools — Triangle Trigonometry & Ambiguous Sine Rule
label.ar: ● Level 2 Analytical Tools — المثلث حساب المثلثات & Ambiguous Sine Rule

body.en:
For any triangle \(ABC\) with side lengths \(a, b, c\) opposite angles \(A, B, C\):

  • Sine Rule: \[ \frac{a}{\sin A} = \frac{b}{\sin B} = \frac{c}{\sin C} = 2R, \] where \(R\) is the circumradius.
  • Ambiguous Case (SSA): When given two sides \(a, b\) and a non-included acute angle \(A\), the altitude from \(C\) is \(h = b\sin A\):
    • If \(a < b\sin A\): no triangle exists (the side is too short to reach the base).
    • If \(a = b\sin A\): exactly one right-angled triangle exists.
    • If \(b\sin A < a < b\): exactly two distinct triangles exist: an acute-angled triangle with \(B_1 = \arcsin\left(\frac{b\sin A}{a}\right)\), and an obtuse-angled triangle with \(B_2 = 180^\circ - B_1\).
    • If \(a \ge b\): exactly one unique triangle exists.
  • Cosine Rule: \[ a^2 = b^2 + c^2 - 2bc\cos A \iff \cos A = \frac{b^2 + c^2 - a^2}{2bc}. \]
  • Triangle Area: \[ \text{Area} = \frac{1}{2}ab\sin C = \frac{1}{2}bc\sin A = \frac{1}{2}ac\sin B. \]
body.ar:
For any المثلث \(ABC\) with side lengths \(a, b, c\) opposite angles \(A, B, C\):

  • Sine Rule: \[ \frac{a}{\sin A} = \frac{b}{\sin B} = \frac{c}{\sin C} = 2R, \] حيث \(R\) is the circumradius.
  • Ambiguous Case (SSA): عندما المعطيات two sides \(a, b\) and a non-included acute الزاوية \(A\), the altitude from \(C\) is \(h = b\sin A\):
    • If \(a < b\sin A\): no المثلث exists (the side is too short to reach the base).
    • If \(a = b\sin A\): exactly one right-angled المثلث exists.
    • If \(b\sin A < a < b\): exactly two distinct triangles exist: an acute-angled المثلث with \(B_1 = \arcsin\left(\frac{b\sin A}{a}\right)\), and an obtuse-angled المثلث with \(B_2 = 180^\circ - B_1\).
    • If \(a \ge b\): exactly one unique المثلث exists.
  • Cosine Rule: \[ a^2 = b^2 + c^2 - 2bc\cos A \iff \cos A = \frac{b^2 + c^2 - a^2}{2bc}. \]
  • Triangle المساحة: \[ \text{Area} = \frac{1}{2}ab\sin C = \frac{1}{2}bc\sin A = \frac{1}{2}ac\sin B. \]

label.en: ● Level 2 Analytical Tools — 2D Vectors & Scalar Dot Product (AA SL)
label.ar: ● Level 2 Analytical Tools — 2D المتجهات & Scalar Dot Product (AA SL)

body.en:
A vector represents a geometric displacement having both magnitude and direction. In 2D Cartesian form:

\[ \mathbf{v} = \begin{pmatrix} v_1 \\ v_2 \end{pmatrix} = v_1 \mathbf{i} + v_2 \mathbf{j}, \quad |\mathbf{v}| = \sqrt{v_1^2 + v_2^2}. \]

Scalar (Dot) Product: For vectors \(\mathbf{u} = \begin{pmatrix} u_1 \\ u_2 \end{pmatrix}\) and \(\mathbf{v} = \begin{pmatrix} v_1 \\ v_2 \end{pmatrix}\):

\[ \mathbf{u} \cdot \mathbf{v} = u_1 v_1 + u_2 v_2 = |\mathbf{u}||\mathbf{v}|\cos\theta, \]

where \(\theta \in [0, \pi]\) is the angle between the vectors.

  • Angle Formula: \[ \cos\theta = \frac{\mathbf{u} \cdot \mathbf{v}}{|\mathbf{u}||\mathbf{v}|} = \frac{u_1 v_1 + u_2 v_2}{\sqrt{u_1^2 + u_2^2}\sqrt{v_1^2 + v_2^2}}. \]
  • Orthogonality Criterion: Non-zero vectors \(\mathbf{u}\) and \(\mathbf{v}\) are perpendicular (\(\theta = \pi/2\)) if and only if: \[ \mathbf{u} \cdot \mathbf{v} = 0. \]
  • Collinearity Criterion: Vectors are parallel if and only if \(\mathbf{u} = k\mathbf{v}\) for some scalar \(k \neq 0\), meaning \(|\mathbf{u} \cdot \mathbf{v}| = |\mathbf{u}||\mathbf{v}|\).
body.ar:
A vector represents a geometric displacement having both magnitude and direction. In 2D Cartesian form:

\[ \mathbf{v} = \begin{pmatrix} v_1 \\ v_2 \end{pmatrix} = v_1 \mathbf{i} + v_2 \mathbf{j}, \quad |\mathbf{v}| = \sqrt{v_1^2 + v_2^2}. \]

  • Angle الصيغة: \[ \cos\theta = \frac{\mathbf{u} \cdot \mathbf{v}}{|\mathbf{u}||\mathbf{v}|} = \frac{u_1 v_1 + u_2 v_2}{\sqrt{u_1^2 + u_2^2}\sqrt{v_1^2 + v_2^2}}. \]

label.en: ● Level 2 Analytical Tools — Sinusoidal Functions & Wave Mechanics
label.ar: ● Level 2 Analytical Tools — Sinusoidal الدوال & Wave Mechanics

body.en:
Periodic physical phenomena (tides, sound waves, seasonal temperatures) are modelled by:

\[ f(t) = A\sin(B(t - C)) + D \quad \text{or} \quad f(t) = A\cos(B(t - C)) + D. \]
  • Amplitude \(|A|\): Half the distance between maximum and minimum values: \[ |A| = \frac{y_{\max} - y_{\min}}{2}. \]
  • Principal Axis / Vertical Translation \(D\): The midline of the oscillation: \[ D = \frac{y_{\max} + y_{\min}}{2}. \]
  • Period \(T\) & Frequency Parameter \(B\): Time taken for one complete cycle: \[ T = \frac{2\pi}{|B|} \iff |B| = \frac{2\pi}{T}. \]
  • Phase Shift \(C\): The horizontal translation shifting the reference curve \(\sin(Bt)\) to the right by \(C\) units.
body.ar:
Periodic physical phenomena (tides, sound waves, seasonal temperatures) are modelled by:

\[ f(t) = A\sin(B(t - C)) + D \quad \text{or} \quad f(t) = A\cos(B(t - C)) + D. \]
  • Amplitude \(|A|\): Half the distance between maximum and minimum values: \[ |A| = \frac{y_{\max} - y_{\min}}{2}. \]
  • Principal Axis / Vertical Translation \(D\): The midline of the oscillation: \[ D = \frac{y_{\max} + y_{\min}}{2}. \]
  • Period \(T\) & Frequency المعامل \(B\): Time taken for one complete cycle: \[ T = \frac{2\pi}{|B|} \iff |B| = \frac{2\pi}{T}. \]
  • Phase Shift \(C\): The horizontal translation shifting the reference curve \(\sin(Bt)\) to the right by \(C\) units.

label.en: ● Level 3 University Rigor — Trigonometric Identities & Exact Equations
label.ar: ● Level 3 University Rigor — Trigonometric المتطابقات & Exact المعادلات

body.en:
Fundamental Pythagorean Identities:

\[ \cos^2\theta + \sin^2\theta = 1, \quad 1 + \tan^2\theta = \sec^2\theta. \]

Double Angle Identities:

\[ \sin 2\theta = 2\sin\theta\cos\theta, \]

and the threefold cosine representation:

\[ \cos 2\theta = \cos^2\theta - \sin^2\theta = 2\cos^2\theta - 1 = 1 - 2\sin^2\theta. \]

Analytical Solution of Trigonometric Equations: When solving equations of the form \(a\cos 2x + b\sin x + c = 0\), substitute \(\cos 2x = 1 - 2\sin^2 x\) to transform into a standard quadratic in \(\sin x\). Always determine the primary reference angle \(\alpha = \arcsin(|k|)\), locate solutions in the required domain (e.g. \([0, 2\pi]\)) according to the quadrant sign of the trigonometric function, and verify boundary conditions.
body.ar:
Fundamental Pythagorean المتطابقات:

\[ \cos^2\theta + \sin^2\theta = 1, \quad 1 + \tan^2\theta = \sec^2\theta. \]

Double الزاوية المتطابقات:

\[ \sin 2\theta = 2\sin\theta\cos\theta, \]

and the threefold cosine representation:

\[ \cos 2\theta = \cos^2\theta - \sin^2\theta = 2\cos^2\theta - 1 = 1 - 2\sin^2\theta. \]

Analytical الحل of Trigonometric المعادلات: عندما solving المعادلات of the form \(a\cos 2x + b\sin x + c = 0\), عوّض \(\cos 2x = 1 - 2\sin^2 x\) to transform into a standard quadratic in \(\sin x\). Always حدّد primary reference الزاوية \(\alpha = \arcsin(|k|)\), locate الحلول in the required المجال (e.g. \([0, 2\pi]\)) according to the quadrant sign of the trigonometric الدالة, and verify boundary conditions.

label.en: ◆ Why It Works — First-Principles Derivation (Geometry & Trigonometry)
label.ar: ◆ لماذا تعمل هذه الطريقة رياضياً — First-Principles اشتقاق (الهندسة & حساب المثلثات)

body.en:
Why the Harmonic \(R\)-Formula & Cosine Rule Hold: Expanding \(R\cos(\theta - \alpha)\) via the compound-angle identity gives:

\[ R\cos(\theta - \alpha) = (R\cos\alpha)\cos\theta + (R\sin\alpha)\sin\theta \]

Matching coefficients with \(a\cos\theta + b\sin\theta\) requires \(R\cos\alpha = a\) and \(R\sin\alpha = b\). Squaring and adding yields \(R^2(\cos^2\alpha + \sin^2\alpha) = a^2 + b^2 \implies R = \sqrt{a^2 + b^2}\), and dividing gives \(\tan\alpha = \dfrac{b}{a}\).
body.ar:
Why the Harmonic \(R\)-الصيغة & Cosine Rule Hold: Expanding \(R\cos(\theta - \alpha)\) via the compound-الزاوية المتطابقة gives:

\[ R\cos(\theta - \alpha) = (R\cos\alpha)\cos\theta + (R\sin\alpha)\sin\theta \]

Matching المعاملات with \(a\cos\theta + b\sin\theta\) requires \(R\cos\alpha = a\) and \(R\sin\alpha = b\). Squaring and adding yields \(R^2(\cos^2\alpha + \sin^2\alpha) = a^2 + b^2 \implies R = \sqrt{a^2 + b^2}\), and dividing gives \(\tan\alpha = \dfrac{b}{a}\).

label.en: Worked Example 3.1 — Exact Sector & Segment Area
label.ar: مثال محلول 3.1 — Exact Sector & Segment المساحة

problem.en:
A circle with centre \(O\) has radius \(r = 6\text{ cm}\). Points \(A\) and \(B\) on the circumference subtend an angle \(\angle AOB = \frac{2\pi}{3}\) radians.
(a) Find the exact perimeter of the shaded sector \(OAB\).
(b) Calculate the exact area of the minor segment enclosed by the chord \(AB\) and the arc \(AB\).
problem.ar:
A الدائرة with centre \(O\) has نصف القطر \(r = 6\text{ cm}\). Points \(A\) and \(B\) on the circumference subtend an الزاوية \(\angle AOB = \frac{2\pi}{3}\) radians.
(a) أوجد exact المحيط of the shaded sector \(OAB\).
(b) احسب exact المساحة of the minor segment enclosed by the chord \(AB\) and the arc \(AB\).

solution.en:
(a) The perimeter of the sector consists of two radii plus the arc length \(s\):
\[ s = r\theta = 6 \times \frac{2\pi}{3} = 4\pi\text{ cm}. \]
Total perimeter: \(P = 2r + s = 2(6) + 4\pi = 12 + 4\pi\text{ cm}\).

(b) Segment area is sector area minus triangle area:
\[ A_{\text{sector}} = \frac{1}{2}r^2\theta = \frac{1}{2}(6^2)\left(\frac{2\pi}{3}\right) = 18 \times \frac{2\pi}{3} = 12\pi\text{ cm}^2. \]
\[ A_{\text{triangle}} = \frac{1}{2}r^2\sin\left(\frac{2\pi}{3}\right) = \frac{1}{2}(36)\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) = 9\sqrt{3}\text{ cm}^2. \]
Exact segment area: \[ A_{\text{segment}} = 12\pi - 9\sqrt{3} = 3(4\pi - 3\sqrt{3})\text{ cm}^2. \]
solution.ar:
(a) The المحيط of the sector consists of two radii plus the arc length \(s\):
\[ s = r\theta = 6 \times \frac{2\pi}{3} = 4\pi\text{ cm}. \]
Total المحيط: \(P = 2r + s = 2(6) + 4\pi = 12 + 4\pi\text{ cm}\).

(b) Segment المساحة is sector المساحة minus المثلث المساحة:
\[ A_{\text{sector}} = \frac{1}{2}r^2\theta = \frac{1}{2}(6^2)\left(\frac{2\pi}{3}\right) = 18 \times \frac{2\pi}{3} = 12\pi\text{ cm}^2. \]
\[ A_{\text{triangle}} = \frac{1}{2}r^2\sin\left(\frac{2\pi}{3}\right) = \frac{1}{2}(36)\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) = 9\sqrt{3}\text{ cm}^2. \]
Exact segment المساحة: \[ A_{\text{segment}} = 12\pi - 9\sqrt{3} = 3(4\pi - 3\sqrt{3})\text{ cm}^2. \]

label.en: Worked Example 3.2 — Ambiguous Case of the Sine Rule
label.ar: مثال محلول 3.2 — Ambiguous Case of the Sine Rule

problem.en:
In triangle \(ABC\), \(a = 8\text{ cm}\), \(b = 10\text{ cm}\), and angle \(A = 35^\circ\).
(a) Show that two distinct triangles can be formed with these dimensions.
(b) Find both possible values for angle \(B\) and the corresponding values for side \(c\).
problem.ar:
In المثلث \(ABC\), \(a = 8\text{ cm}\), \(b = 10\text{ cm}\), and الزاوية \(A = 35^\circ\).
(a) Show that two distinct triangles can be formed with these dimensions.
(b) Find both possible values for الزاوية \(B\) and the corresponding values for side \(c\).

solution.en:
(a) Calculate the altitude from \(C\):
\[ h = b\sin A = 10\sin 35^\circ \approx 10(0.5736) = 5.736\text{ cm}. \]
Since \(h < a < b\) (i.e. \(5.736 < 8 < 10\)), the side \(a\) can swing across the altitude to meet the base at two distinct points. Hence, two distinct triangles exist. ∎

(b) Apply the sine rule:
\[ \frac{\sin B}{b} = \frac{\sin A}{a} \implies \sin B = \frac{10\sin 35^\circ}{8} \approx \frac{5.7358}{8} \approx 0.7170. \]
Acute angle solution: \(B_1 = \arcsin(0.7170) \approx 45.8^\circ\).
Obtuse angle solution: \(B_2 = 180^\circ - 45.8^\circ = 134.2^\circ\).
Check angle sum for triangle 2: \(A + B_2 = 35^\circ + 134.2^\circ = 169.2^\circ < 180^\circ\), which is valid.

Find side \(c\) for each case:
Case 1: \(C_1 = 180^\circ - (35^\circ + 45.8^\circ) = 99.2^\circ\).
\[ c_1 = \frac{a\sin C_1}{\sin A} = \frac{8\sin 99.2^\circ}{\sin 35^\circ} \approx \frac{8(0.9871)}{0.5736} \approx 13.77\text{ cm}. \]
Case 2: \(C_2 = 180^\circ - (35^\circ + 134.2^\circ) = 10.8^\circ\).
\[ c_2 = \frac{a\sin C_2}{\sin A} = \frac{8\sin 10.8^\circ}{\sin 35^\circ} \approx \frac{8(0.1874)}{0.5736} \approx 2.61\text{ cm}. \]
solution.ar:
(a) احسب altitude from \(C\):
\[ h = b\sin A = 10\sin 35^\circ \approx 10(0.5736) = 5.736\text{ cm}. \]
Since \(h < a < b\) (i.e. \(5.736 < 8 < 10\)), the side \(a\) can swing across the altitude to meet the base at two distinct points. ومنه, two distinct triangles exist. ∎

(b) Apply the sine rule:
\[ \frac{\sin B}{b} = \frac{\sin A}{a} \implies \sin B = \frac{10\sin 35^\circ}{8} \approx \frac{5.7358}{8} \approx 0.7170. \]
Acute الزاوية الحل: \(B_1 = \arcsin(0.7170) \approx 45.8^\circ\).
Obtuse الزاوية الحل: \(B_2 = 180^\circ - 45.8^\circ = 134.2^\circ\).
Check الزاوية sum for المثلث 2: \(A + B_2 = 35^\circ + 134.2^\circ = 169.2^\circ < 180^\circ\), which is valid.

Find side \(c\) for each case:
Case 1: \(C_1 = 180^\circ - (35^\circ + 45.8^\circ) = 99.2^\circ\).
\[ c_1 = \frac{a\sin C_1}{\sin A} = \frac{8\sin 99.2^\circ}{\sin 35^\circ} \approx \frac{8(0.9871)}{0.5736} \approx 13.77\text{ cm}. \]
Case 2: \(C_2 = 180^\circ - (35^\circ + 134.2^\circ) = 10.8^\circ\).
\[ c_2 = \frac{a\sin C_2}{\sin A} = \frac{8\sin 10.8^\circ}{\sin 35^\circ} \approx \frac{8(0.1874)}{0.5736} \approx 2.61\text{ cm}. \]

label.en: Worked Example 3.3 — 2D Vector Orthogonality & Parameter Determination
label.ar: مثال محلول 3.3 — 2D المتجه Orthogonality & المعامل Determination

problem.en:
Let \(\mathbf{u} = \begin{pmatrix} 2k - 1 \\ 3 \end{pmatrix}\) and \(\mathbf{v} = \begin{pmatrix} 4 \\ k + 2 \end{pmatrix}\).
(a) Find the values of \(k\) for which \(\mathbf{u}\) is perpendicular to \(\mathbf{v}\).
(b) For \(k = 2\), compute the exact angle \(\theta\) between \(\mathbf{u}\) and \(\mathbf{v}\).
problem.ar:
Let \(\mathbf{u} = \begin{pmatrix} 2k - 1 \\ 3 \end{pmatrix}\) and \(\mathbf{v} = \begin{pmatrix} 4 \\ k + 2 \end{pmatrix}\).
(a) أوجد values of \(k\) for which \(\mathbf{u}\) is perpendicular to \(\mathbf{v}\).
(b) For \(k = 2\), compute the exact الزاوية \(\theta\) between \(\mathbf{u}\) and \(\mathbf{v}\).

solution.en:
(a) \(\mathbf{u} \perp \mathbf{v} \iff \mathbf{u} \cdot \mathbf{v} = 0\):
\[ (2k - 1)(4) + 3(k + 2) = 0 \implies 8k - 4 + 3k + 6 = 0 \implies 11k + 2 = 0 \implies k = -\frac{2}{11}. \]

(b) When \(k = 2\):
\(\mathbf{u} = \begin{pmatrix} 3 \\ 3 \end{pmatrix}\) and \(\mathbf{v} = \begin{pmatrix} 4 \\ 4 \end{pmatrix}\).
Notice that \(\mathbf{v} = \frac{4}{3}\mathbf{u}\). Both vectors point in the identical direction along the line \(y = x\).
Verify with dot product: \(|\mathbf{u}| = \sqrt{3^2 + 3^2} = 3\sqrt{2}\), \(|\mathbf{v}| = \sqrt{4^2 + 4^2} = 4\sqrt{2}\).
\[ \mathbf{u} \cdot \mathbf{v} = 3(4) + 3(4) = 24. \]
\[ \cos\theta = \frac{24}{(3\sqrt{2})(4\sqrt{2})} = \frac{24}{24} = 1 \implies \theta = 0\text{ rad} = 0^\circ. \]

body.en:
GDC Angle Mode Setting: Calculus and circle formulae (\(s = r\theta\), \(A = \frac{1}{2}r^2\theta\)) require Radian mode. Forgetting to switch between Degrees and Radians causes cascading accuracy mark deductions across Paper 2.

Ambiguous Case Obligation: Whenever given SSA (two sides and a non-included angle) where the side opposite the angle is shorter than the adjacent side, always test whether \(180^\circ - B_1\) leaves room for the third angle. Omitting the second triangle forfeits half the question marks.

Double Angle Inversion: When substituting \(\cos 2x\), choose the identity strategically: use \(1 - 2\sin^2 x\) if the rest of the equation contains \(\sin x\), and \(2\cos^2 x - 1\) if it contains \(\cos x\).

question.en: Practice 3.1: Solve the equation \(2\cos 2x = 4\cos x - 3\) for \(0 \le x \le 2\pi\), giving exact solutions.
question.ar: Practice 3.1: حل المعادلة \(2\cos 2x = 4\cos x - 3\) for \(0 \le x \le 2\pi\), giving exact solutions.

solution.en:
1. Substitute the double angle identity \(\cos 2x = 2\cos^2 x - 1\):
\[ 2(2\cos^2 x - 1) = 4\cos x - 3 \implies 4\cos^2 x - 2 = 4\cos x - 3 \implies 4\cos^2 x - 4\cos x + 1 = 0. \]
2. Recognize the perfect square: \((2\cos x - 1)^2 = 0 \implies 2\cos x - 1 = 0 \implies \cos x = \frac{1}{2}\).
3. Reference angle: \(\alpha = \arccos(1/2) = \frac{\pi}{3}\).
Cosine is positive in Quadrants I and IV:
In Q1: \(x = \frac{\pi}{3}\).
In Q4: \(x = 2\pi - \frac{\pi}{3} = \frac{5\pi}{3}\).
Exact solutions: \(x \in \left\{ \frac{\pi}{3}, \frac{5\pi}{3} \right\}\).

question.en: Practice 3.2: Ship \(A\) leaves port \(P\) on a bearing of \(040^\circ\) traveling at \(15\text{ km/h}\). At the same time, ship \(B\) leaves \(P\) on a bearing of \(130^\circ\) traveling at \(20\text{ km/h}\). Find the distance between the two ships after 2 hours.
question.ar: Practice 3.2: Ship \(A\) leaves port \(P\) on a bearing of \(040^\circ\) traveling at \(15\text{ km/h}\). At the same time, ship \(B\) leaves \(P\) on a bearing of \(130^\circ\) traveling at \(20\text{ km/h}\). أوجد distance between the two ships after 2 hours.

solution.en:
1. Distance travelled by ship \(A\): \(d_A = 15 \times 2 = 30\text{ km}\).
2. Distance travelled by ship \(B\): \(d_B = 20 \times 2 = 40\text{ km}\).
3. The angle between their paths is the difference in bearings: \(\theta = 130^\circ - 40^\circ = 90^\circ\).
4. Since the triangle is right-angled at \(P\), apply the Pythagorean theorem (or Cosine Rule with \(\cos 90^\circ = 0\)):
\[ d = \sqrt{30^2 + 40^2} = \sqrt{900 + 1600} = \sqrt{2500} = 50\text{ km}. \]
The distance between the ships after 2 hours is exactly 50 km.

question.en: [Practice 3 · Easy] In the diagram, triangle ABC is shown with coordinates A(1, 1), B(3, 1), and C(3, 5). What is the exact length of the side AC in simplest radical form?
question.ar: حل المسألة التالية في (Geometry & Trigonometry): [Practice 3 · Easy] In the diagram, triangle ABC is shown with coordinates A(1, 1), B(3, 1), and C(3, 5). What is the exact length of the side AC in simplest radical form?

hints.en: Using the distance formula between \( A(1, 1) \) and \( C(3, 5) \): \(AC = \sqrt{(3 - 1)^2 + (5 - 1)^2}\).
hints.ar: باستخدام distance formula between \( A(1, 1) \) and \( C(3, 5) \): \(AC = \sqrt{(3 - 1)^2 + (5 - 1)^2}\).

solution.en: Using the distance formula between \( A(1, 1) \) and \( C(3, 5) \): \[ AC = \sqrt{(3 - 1)^2 + (5 - 1)^2} = \sqrt{2^2 + 4^2} = \sqrt{4 + 16} = \sqrt{20} = 2\sqrt{5}. \]

question.en: [Practice 4 · Easy] In the given triangle ABC, AB = 10, AC = 15, and BD = 6. D is a point on BC such that AD is the angle bisector of angle BAC. Find the length of DC.
question.ar: [Practice 4 · Easy] In the given triangle ABC, AB = 10, AC = 15, and BD = 6. D is a point on BC such that AD is the angle bisector of angle BAC. أوجد length of DC.

hints.en: By the Angle Bisector Theorem, the ratio of the sides adjacent to the angle bisector is equal to the ratio of the segments created by the bisector on the opposite side. Therefore, \(\frac{AB}{AC} = \frac{BD}{DC}\).
hints.ar: بتطبيق Angle Bisector Theorem, the ratio of the sides adjacent to the angle bisector is equal to the ratio of the segments created بتطبيق bisector on the opposite side. وبالتالي، \(\frac{AB}{AC} = \frac{BD}{DC}\).

hints.en: Substituting the given values, we get \(\frac{10}{15} = \frac{6}{DC}\). Simplifying the left side, \(\frac{2}{3} = \frac{6}{DC}\). Cross-multiplying, \(2 \times DC = 3 \times 6\). \(2 \times DC = 18\).
